scientific_question: Can a simple learned software model distinguish identical content recurring as distinct observed episodes, plans, memory-references, and continuous events, while an independent external clock fixes chronology? This does NOT test whether consciousness is timeless.
observables: physical event identity from independent witnessed event_id
observed physical occurrence vs planned future occurrence
reference clock and local civil-day label
remembered or described episode reference with provenance
continuous physical event vs discrete recurrence

training_contract.selection: Hyperparameters frozen before heldout evaluation; no test-driven tuning.
training_contract.baseline: Most frequent class in balanced synthetic toy dataset
training_contract.target: Heldout accuracy >= 0.90 and zero prospective-to-observed misclassifications
training_contract.clock_policy: Timezone-aware UTC physical timestamps with separate Europe/Kyiv civil dates; planned next-day items never reclassified as already observed
training_contract.model_scope: EVENT-METADATA LEARNING ONLY; DOES NOT LEARN A MENTAL STATE OR HUMAN MEMORY
training_contract.deployment: Artifact JSON in GitHub Actions only; no weights in production; merge research-only code after CI if appropriate

mandatory_abstentions: Identical content without event ID/witness cannot prove one physical event or multiple repeats
Reported memory without event timestamps cannot establish objective ordering
Tomorrow's prediction or planned replay is not an observed future event
Civil-calendar day labels change with reference context without altering objective event identity
Task performance cannot demonstrate qualia or physical timelessness
comparison_notes: R2/R2B cognitive four-trial synthetic demonstrators are separate from R4 event metadata training.
R4 training accuracy estimates only agreement with a synthetic generator; it is not evidence that Alzheimer patients can identify temporal recurrence.
No human participant data have been obtained via R3. External data request remains on its own tracked issue.
